meta_disclaimer: Drift Zone scoring mechanics + technique, verified against independent sources (game8, GamesRadar, Steam community). Car prices confirmed on game8. Technique is stable driving-model knowledge, not patch-sensitive.

concept.headline: A sliding car goes where its MOMENTUM carries it — not where the front wheels point.
points: MOMENTUM = the car's actual direction of travel. It keeps arcing through the corner and changes slowly (it's a heavy object in motion).
NOSE ANGLE = where the car points. It's swung sideways because the REAR tyres lost grip and slid out.
The FRONT tyres still grip. Countersteering (turning toward the slide) makes them pull against the spin — it CATCHES the rear so you don't spin, it does NOT send you the wrong way.
Throttle is your ANGLE dial: more gas = more angle/rotation, less gas = the rear regains grip and the car straightens. You feather it.
To end a drift: ease off throttle so the rear grips again, then centre the wheel. The car only slides when you provoke it.

scoring.multiplier_note: The multiplier grows EXPONENTIALLY the longer you hold ONE unbroken slide. Straightening the wheel resets it to zero. A single long chain beats many short drifts — one 600K slide > three 200K slides.
scoring.entry: Enter already sideways: tap the handbrake + flick the wheel just BEFORE the start line, ~50–80 mph, so you're at full angle the instant scoring begins.
scoring.width: Use the full width of the road. Wider, bigger-angle slides score far more than tight narrow ones.

failure_modes.symptom: You spin out and end up backwards
failure_modes.cause: Too much throttle + not enough countersteer → the rear rotates past the point you can catch it.
failure_modes.fix: Ease OFF the throttle and add MORE countersteer (steer into the slide), and catch it early — small correction beats a big one.

failure_modes.symptom: You run out of speed / it straightens
failure_modes.cause: Too much angle (sideways tyres scrub off your speed), or you lifted fully off the gas.
failure_modes.fix: Reduce the angle (point more forward) and FEED IN more throttle to keep momentum.

settings_checklist: Traction Control: OFF (it kills the wheelspin you need)
Stability Control: OFF (it auto-straightens the car and fights your angle)
Stay in 2nd or 3rd gear mid-drift — too low a gear = snappy wheelspin that spins you
Smooth inputs — stab the throttle or yank the wheel and you snap around
practice_drill: Skip scored zones for 10 min. On a long empty road, get the rear out and hold ONE steady slide in a straight line using only countersteer + throttle feathering. Rear steps out too far → ease gas + add counter; it starts to straighten → add gas. Hold it a few seconds, then take that same balance through corners — and never straighten the wheel between them.

tune.easiest: Don't hand-tune your first drift car. In Upgrade & Tune → Find Tuning Setups, download a top-rated DRIFT tune for the car — it installs the angle kit, drift diff and tyres and sets the sliders.
tune.manual_essentials: RWD · steering-angle upgrade · rear differential ~100% accel / low decel · rear tyre pressure a bit higher than front · ~400–600 hp (over-powering makes it uncontrollable, not better).

scoring_mechanics.researched: 2026-08-10 (79-agent deep dive; corroboration bar RELAXED per player — tiers: corroborated / single-source / fh5-inherited)

mechanics.name: Chain multiplier
mechanics.facts: Grows continuously while ONE slide stays unbroken; resets on straightening, spinning out, or dropping below the slip-angle threshold. HUD-observed reaching x6.8→x7.6+ during continuous drifting (single-source video). The actual growth CURVE (rate/steps/cap timing) is publicly unknown.

mechanics.name: Banking rules
mechanics.facts: Drift Zone points accrue only during the active run and bank when you cross the finish gate — what happens after (spin/crash) is irrelevant (single-source). Rewind PRESERVES accrued zone score, but too many rewinds fails the attempt. Skill chains bank on stopping or changing cars; ~50,000 chain score = 1 skill point. Enter the first gate already sideways — pre-gate chain feeds the multiplier at entry.

mechanics.name: Wall contact — CONTRADICTORY
mechanics.facts: Guides uniformly claim ANY solid contact zeroes the combo (no light-tap tolerance). But video evidence shows fence/tree hits mid-run with no visible ZONE-score reset, and FH5 had a 'Drift Tap' skill (~1,000 pts) for glancing wall touches that did NOT break the chain — Drift Tap is confirmed to exist in FH6. Best model: SKILL-CHAIN and ZONE-SCORE respond to contact differently, and nobody has isolated which resets when. In-game test would settle it.

mechanics.name: Angle behavior
mechanics.facts: A minimum slip angle gates scoring — shallow four-wheel slides score nothing (single-source). Scoring weights angle + duration over speed; past-90-degree drifts still score (a 90-degree slide held 15s outscores a briefer 120-degree one). Exact minimum angle and any cap: unknown.

mechanics.name: Speed floor
mechanics.facts: No FH6 minimum speed is documented anywhere; runs visibly score at 30-42 mph, one 3-star run stayed in 1st gear throughout, and slow-donut exploits work (no route validation, no forward-progress requirement — players loop one corner to inflate score before crossing the finish). FH5 baseline was ~40 km/h (~25 mph).

mechanics.name: Transitions / manji
mechanics.facts: Direction-change spamming is heavily rewarded with NO technical-purity gate — swaying left-right repeatedly scores near-identically to skilled linked drifting. No source documents a DISCRETE transition bonus; the reward comes from keeping one chain alive. No reverse-entry bonus exists in any FH6 or FH5 source.

mechanics.name: Zone star thresholds
mechanics.facts: 20 Drift Zones with FIXED per-zone 3-star targets: 45,000 (Inner City Run, easiest) to 340,000 (Hakone Nanamagari, hardest). No evidence thresholds scale with car class/PI — BUT an official v398.92.0 note says PR Stunt scoring is 'bucketed by Car Class', which sits unresolved against the fixed-threshold model. Zones are untimed: pure point targets per single run.

mechanics.name: Horizon Drifting Sessions
mechanics.facts: Officially named mode (Jul 20 patch fixed sessions 'ending abruptly', FH6BR-3988). Championship-style: highest score wins, not a race; entered via Horizon Play; a 'Custom Drifting' variant allows private lobbies with host-set class/drivetrain rules (corroborated incl. official progression article). The mode's internal scoring rules: ZERO public documentation.

mechanics.name: Car skill multipliers
mechanics.facts: Wikis conflict (default chain cap 5x vs 7x; FD cars 7x perk single-source; 22B-STI 9x 'highest in game') — but OUR OWN farm data independently matches the 5x-default / 22B-9x model (measured: 9x needs ~56k score for the 10-SP cap vs ~100k at 5x). Treat 5x default, FD 7x, 22B 9x as the working model. FH5 prior: Hoonicorn 8x.

mechanics.name: Assists
mechanics.facts: TCS/STM off + manual shifting are CAPABILITY requirements, not score modifiers — no source documents any assist-based score bonus/penalty (an FH5-era +35%/+50% claim was REJECTED as fabricated in verification). One n=1 experiment: 8 straight zone failures on automatic, first-try 3-star after switching to manual. Clutch-kick on Manual w/Clutch was broken until Jul 20 (FH6BR-15302).

mechanics.name: E-brake vs power-slide
mechanics.facts: No FH6 source documents a scoring difference by initiation type. FH5 tracked 'Drift' and 'E-Drift' as separate skills at the same 100-pt base. Settleable in one session (see experiments).

mechanics.name: Surface effects
mechanics.facts: One n=1 report: a dirt-road Drift Zone effectively unscoreable in WINTER ('really bugged in winter', ~3h of failed attempts). FH5 baseline: drift skills score on any surface. Season may matter more than surface in FH6.

mechanics.name: Co-op LINK bonus
mechanics.facts: Twin Drift LINK: drift parallel with a teammate 5+ seconds in shared sessions → score x2. FH6-native co-op mechanic worth testing in convoy.

mechanics.name: Upcoming: Drift Attack
mechanics.facts: A NEW mode named 'Drift Attack' debuts hands-on at gamescom (Aug 26-30, 2026, official Xbox announcement) — expect drift scoring news around then; re-sweep after.

experiments: SPEED FLOOR (~2 min): hold a steady e-brake slide on flat asphalt, bleed speed slowly, note the HUD speed where points stop ticking.

INITIATION TYPES (1 session): same corner, same car — e-brake entry, power-slide entry, reverse entry; read the skill popup names and compare points for equal slides. Settles three empty mechanics at once.

WALL CONTACT ISOLATION: inside a zone, take one deliberate glancing wall tap mid-slide — watch BOTH the skill-chain popup (Drift Tap? chain break?) and the zone points ticker separately. Resolves the guides-vs-video contradiction.
MULTIPLIER CURVE: screen-record one long unbroken slide with the HUD multiplier visible; the x-vs-time trace IS the curve nobody has published.

drift_tuning.phase_model: Drift has its own five phases: INITIATION (breaking traction) -> ANGLE (rotating to target) -> HOLD (throttle=angle dial, countersteer catches) -> TRANSITION (weight swap between directions) -> EXIT (straighten, rehook).

slider_map.why: Leans the steering axis back for self-centering - the wheel snaps back and 'catches' the slide during countersteer and transitions; adds dynamic camber with steering angle.
Pre-tilts the tire so the FULL contact patch lands flat at full countersteer lock - more front bite = more angle held without washing out.
Driven tires keep a predictable hookup angle while sliding.
Speeds initiation and improves countersteer geometry - the inside wheel already points where you want to go mid-slide.
Zero lets the rear swing freely; a touch of toe-in adds spin resistance in transitions.

'Your stiffer end loses grip first' - soft front keeps the outside front planted for countersteer; stiff rear breaks traction willingly and holds angle. (Minority school: everything ~95% stiff for snap response.)

slider_map.setting: SOFT overall (~400/400, or 350-400F/250-300R), slammed, rear 1-2 clicks HIGHER
slider_map.why: Soft = progressive, forgiving weight transfer; a stiff drift car 'changes direction violently and spins'. Rear-high rake leans static weight forward for rotation.

slider_map.setting: Two schools: rebound=spring slider + bump=60% (FH5-inherited formula) vs flat-soft 4.0 everywhere (forza.tools FH6)
slider_map.why: Both schools agree: stiff damping = violent side-to-side snap. Stiffen rear rebound slightly if transitions whip too fast.
THE strongest consensus in drift tuning and identical to our prior doctrine: locked-under-power rear spins both wheels together for sustainable slides; low decel frees lift-off rotation.

slider_map.setting: CONTESTED: rear-higher camp (30-32R/26-28F, statically cut rear grip) vs front-higher camp (F30-33/R19-27 - underinflate rears, wheelspin heat raises them to ~30-32 equilibrium)
slider_map.why: Same goal (less rear grip, predictable breakaway), opposite mechanisms. Our old 'rear PSI > front' doctrine DOWNGRADED to contested - A/B test queued.

slider_map.setting: CONTESTED: front 60-62% + lowered pressure (weight forward, rear swings, e-brake corrects) vs rear ~45% (lock rears to initiate)

slider_map.why: Front downforce feeds countersteer grip; rear downforce fights the slide.
Enough to sustain wheelspin at angle, not so much the rears are overwhelmed.

awd_drifting.verdict: VIABLE and community-standard for drift-ZONE farming and dirt zones; RWD remains the style/competitive skill standard.

settings.center: 75-100% rear (90 the common quote; below ~75 the front 'pulls you straight')
settings.front_diff: unsettled two schools: locked-ish 100/30 vs wide open with only 3-5% front power as 'anti-spin-out insurance'

awd_drifting.feel: The most forgiving drift config - the front axle's slight pull points the car, initiates on demand, and acts as spin-out insurance. Trades away max angle and style purity.
awd_drifting.when: Zone star-farming (thresholds 45k-340k), dirt/offroad drift zones (rally tires + AWD confirmed repeatedly), long fast zones IF speed scores (scoring dispute unresolved). Community AWD picks: FD Fairlady Z 'AWD Powerbuild', Honda Acty, F-150 Lariat FE, 22B, rally-suspension Ultima.

parts.drift_springs_dampers: Auto-slams (-2.55in on the Viper vs -0.94 stock), unlocks suspension tuning, and is PROBABLY the 'angle kit' - one source: 'Drift Suspension unlocks maximum steering lock'. NO separate angle-kit part exists anywhere (three enumerated loadouts + our own menu captures). A/B test = top of the queue.
parts.drift_diff: Unlocks full diff tuning; preset reportedly 100/10; a tuned Race 2-way is functionally equivalent.
parts.drift_transmission_4speed: Fewer, longer gears - live in 3rd and flutter throttle. OPTIONAL (race 6/7-speed fine). CAVEAT: if clutch-kick requires non-race transmissions (single-source claim), Drift/Race boxes may forfeit it - test #4.
parts.drift_compound: Predictable breakaway; whether it beats drag/snow compounds for lowest asphalt grip is CONTESTED.

doctrine_changes: 'RWD + angle kit' RESCOPED: RWD for style/competitive; AWD 75-100% rear verified for zones/dirt. 'Angle kit' as a part name RETIRED - operationally it means Drift Springs & Dampers.
'Rear PSI > front' DOWNGRADED to contested (credible front-higher heat-soak camp).
'Diff ~100 accel / low decel' CONFIRMED and strengthened (identical on AWD rear diffs).
